title: An FPT Algorithm for Maximum-Weight Independent Set in Embedded Graphs, in Lean 4
abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of a fixed-parameter theorem of "Maximum-weight independent set in embedded graphs parameterized by Euler genus and number of odd faces" (forthcoming), with a provably correct implementation of the algorithm as one fixed program for an explicit sixteen-register pointer machine. Lean proves that for every graph drawn in a closed surface of Euler genus gamma whose complement has k regions of odd total boundary length, and all integer vertex weights, the program outputs a maximum-weight independent set within 2^(c (p size(p) + 1)) (N size(M))^c bit operations, where p = gamma + k, N = |V| + |E| + 1, M = max(1, max |w_v|), size(x) is the binary length of x and c is an absolute constant; that is, 2^O(p log(p+1)) poly(N, log(M+1)) with an absolute polynomial exponent. Surfaces are represented by finite combinatorial flag maps; orientable and nonorientable surfaces, disconnected and noncellular drawings, loops, multiple edges, isolated vertices and negative weights are covered. The algorithm solves one exact linear program per retained component over a finite-group network whose size depends only on p, using exact integral quotient coordinates, midpoint convexity of class minima and a coarse Jensen inequality, and recovers an optimal set from perturbed edge costs. The cost is a logarithmic bit-cost measure including an explicit stack simulation of recursive calls. The proofs use exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
